page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical Intel Xeon 8375C cores running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 4096.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided via a 3800 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 123925.38 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16209.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 302.32 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 122.18 GB/sec for large block write operations. The CPU features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration, contributing to a top-tier Passmark CPU encryption score of 110669.62 and a top-tier ray tracing score of 100661.0.

While multi-threaded and memory-intensive tasks perform in the top tiers, single-core performance remains average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1690.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1893.7. Additionally, without dedicated GPU hardware, large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, yielding a weak 2.76 tokens/sec on 70B models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of DDR4 memory relative to compute resources makes this instance profile suitable for memory-bound enterprise workloads rather than raw single-threaded compute.

This instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and enterprise applications. The strong database operations score of 29714.26 and Redis SET throughput of 106.84 million operations per second support its deployment for high-throughput transactional databases, real-time analytics, and memory-heavy ETL pipelines.
